headline: Shipping slows to near standstill in Strait of Hormuz after tanker attacks
summary: Traffic dropped from over 130 ships daily to just five on Saturday, as US-Iran talks stall and tensions escalate in the Middle East.
details: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has ground to a near standstill following attacks on tankers and stalled US-Iran negotiations to resolve the Middle East conflict.
Data from Kpler shows that only five commodity vessels transited the strait on Saturday, with none registered for Sunday, compared to 31 in the previous weekend.
Before the war launched by the US and Israel on Iran in February, the waterway handled a fifth of the world's crude oil and liquefied natural gas shipments, typically seeing over 130 ships a day.
The slowdown follows reports from the United Arab Emirates that three vessels operated by the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company were attacked in transit last week.

The United States has stated it could maintain a naval blockade of Iran indefinitely, while Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi stated that Washington must meet Iran's conditions for shipping to resume.

In a separate development, shipping at the Bab el-Mandeb strait has also decreased, with 49 weekend transits by commodity vessels, down from 55 the prior week, following a Houthi naval blockade on Saudi Arabia.
caption:
From 130 ships a day to almost zero. The Strait of Hormuz is grinding to a halt.

Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has ground to a near standstill following attacks on tankers and stalled US-Iran negotiations to resolve the Middle East conflict.

Data from Kpler shows that only five commodity vessels transited the strait on Saturday, with none registered for Sunday, compared to 31 in the previous weekend.

Before the war launched by the US and Israel on Iran in February, the waterway handled a fifth of the world's crude oil and liquefied natural gas shipments, typically seeing over 130 ships a day.

The slowdown follows reports from the United Arab Emirates that three vessels operated by the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company were attacked in transit last week.

The United States has stated it could maintain a naval blockade of Iran indefinitely, while Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi stated that Washington must meet Iran's conditions for shipping to resume.

In a separate development, shipping at the Bab el-Mandeb strait has also decreased, with 49 weekend transits by commodity vessels, down from 55 the prior week, following a Houthi naval blockade on Saudi Arabia.

headline_marked: Australia coach admits [[Bangladesh victory was hard to accept]] after poor performance
headline: Australia coach admits Bangladesh victory was hard to accept after poor performance
summary: Andrew McDonald admits the team failed to maintain their standards after a crushing defeat to Bangladesh in Darwin.
details: Bangladesh secured a historic first Test victory in Australia, dominating the match in Darwin over three and a half days.
Australia struggled throughout, trailing by 226 runs after their first innings total of 198, and could only set a target of 57 runs in the second innings.
Bangladesh chased down the target, winning by 9 wickets to seal the victory.
Australian head coach Andrew McDonald described the performance as 'very bad,' stating it was hard to accept scoring under 500 runs across two innings on that wicket.
The defeat has sparked calls for change within the Australian squad, with legend Ricky Ponting suggesting a need for changes in the opening and number three positions.
Many former cricketers are now calling for the inclusion of the next generation of players, noting that only Cameron Green was under 30 among the playing XI.
Coach McDonald acknowledged the discussions about age balance and squad changes, stating that a loss often intensifies such conversations.
Despite the calls for change, McDonald expressed belief that the current players still have plenty of cricket left in them.
caption:
A historic win for Bangladesh and a crushing blow for Australia. Coach Andrew McDonald admits they simply failed their own standards.

Bangladesh secured a historic first Test victory in Australia, dominating the match in Darwin over three and a half days.

Australia struggled throughout, trailing by 226 runs after their first innings total of 198, and could only set a target of 57 runs in the second innings.

Bangladesh chased down the target, winning by 9 wickets to seal the victory.

Australian head coach Andrew McDonald described the performance as 'very bad,' stating it was hard to accept scoring under 500 runs across two innings on that wicket.

The defeat has sparked calls for change within the Australian squad, with legend Ricky Ponting suggesting a need for changes in the opening and number three positions.

Many former cricketers are now calling for the inclusion of the next generation of players, noting that only Cameron Green was under 30 among the playing XI.

Coach McDonald acknowledged the discussions about age balance and squad changes, stating that a loss often intensifies such conversations.

Despite the calls for change, McDonald expressed belief that the current players still have plenty of cricket left in them.
